payoff: PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35 (21 October 2026) fix two critical flaws that can let a request with no login run code on your server; php.net says updating is the only safe choice.

alternatives.spoken: [fired up] PHP itself says no setting fully protects your server.
[urgent] Two critical PHP bugs, (break) [serious] and a request with no login runs code.
[excited] PHP shipped fixes for two critical bugs (break) [serious] on October twenty first.

points.title: No setting fixes
points.body: Only an update fully fixes it

caption:
PHP2Shell: critical PHP remote code execution flaws, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619
Fixed in PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35 on 21 October 2026. Source: the php.net security advisory.
Which PHP version runs your server? 👇
voiceover: [urgent] One request, no login, (break) [serious] and the attack can start before your code runs.
[serious] Two critical bugs let attackers run code.
[firm] PHP says only updating fixes it, (break) [serious] no setting does.
[confident and fast] The fixes shipped October twenty first.
[warm, curious] So what does your server run?

scenes.title: Security advisory
scenes.text: We consider the risk highest for mod_php, with a demonstrated exploit where an unauthenticated request can trigger the attack before any application code runs.

scenes.title: PHP 8.5.12 Released!
scenes.text: There are no complete mitigations, updating is the only safe choice.
scenes.mark: updating is the only safe choice
